name: Steel Deck Plate
desc: An industrial tread-plate deck running out to a hazed horizon — raised lozenges flipping direction course by course, plates butted on welded seams and studded with countersunk bolts, rust bloom and oil soaked into the tread — while an unseen beacon sweeps its wedge across the deck and every lozenge crown takes the light in turn.

energy.doc: how hard the beacon and the sheen burn on the tread

scale.doc: perspective spread of the deck — plate and tread size follow it

density.doc: how fine the tread pattern is, and how many plates and bolts make up the deck

wear.doc: rust bloom, oil soak, and how much tread corrosion has eaten away

speed.doc: beacon rotation and sheen drift rate

hue.doc: steel hue (210 = cold plant steel; rust and hazard paint answer on the complement)

y.doc: horizon line y — nothing is ever painted above it

alpha.doc: opacity of the beacon, sheen and haze

style.doc: treadplate: raw industrial steel, modelled lozenges throwing their own shadows, rust and oil worked in · patina: corroded through — the tread eaten away in patches, dark and abandoned, iron gone to rust · hazard: the graphic language of safety — chevrons and keep-clear lines painted under the tread in flat bold colour · anodised: clinical coloured metal, saturated and clean, no grime at all — a product shot rather than a workplace

act.doc: drift: the beacon turns steadily · alarm: it spins up — the wedge whips round the deck · shutdown: the beacon almost stops and the deck goes quiet

seed.doc: deterministic seed for tread tone, corrosion, oil and bolt placement
